meta.title: Italy 2026
meta.subtitle: Rome · Florence · Tuscany · Amalfi · Naples
meta.arrival: FCO Mon Aug 24, 11:50am (ITA Airways from IAH)
meta.routeLine: Rome (3) → Florence (2) → Tuscany (3) → Amalfi (3) → Naples (1) → Rome finale (1)
meta.transportLine: Self-drive rental, FCO to FCO (Aug 24 – Sep 6) — Benz C-Class or similar, IDP in hand
meta.chainStory: Hotel Trame (Rome, independent) → Casa G. Firenze (Florence, Michelin Guide) → Il Castelfalfi (Tuscany, TUI Blue Selection) → Anantara Convento (Amalfi, Minor / GHA) → De Bonart (Naples, Hilton Curio) → The St. Regis Rome (Marriott Bonvoy)

days.title: Landing in Rome
days.kicker: ROME — Hotel Trame, by the Pantheon
days.note: Jet-lag day. Nothing ticketed, nothing timed — the only fixed point is dinner.

items.title: Land at FCO
items.detail: Immigration + bags, about 45 min

items.title: Pick up the rental car
items.detail: Benz C-Class or similar, automatic — reservation #21586310US4. Have the IDP and licence ready.

items.title: Drive to a garage near the hotel
items.detail: Hotel Trame sits inside Rome's ZTL — park in a garage just outside it (e.g. near Largo Argentina) and walk in. The car stays there until Day 4.

items.title: Check in at Hotel Trame
items.detail: A former Franciscan monastery a few streets off Campo de' Fiori

items.title: First walk: Pantheon → Piazza Navona → Campo de' Fiori
items.detail: The Pantheon is an eight-minute walk. Go before the nap, not after.

items.title: Nap, deliberately
items.detail: Set an alarm. This is the single best defence against day-two jet lag.

items.title: Aperitivo at Etabli
items.detail: Or the Campari bar on Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Dinner — Armando al Pantheon
items.detail: Tiny, family-run, and booked out weeks ahead. Reserve now.

days.title: The Vatican, before anyone else
days.note: Early entry is the whole point: the Sistine Chapel is a different room with 40 people in it than with 400.

items.title: Vatican early-entry private tour
items.detail: Into the Sistine Chapel before general admission

items.title: Lunch — Da Romolo or Hostaria Dino e Tony
items.detail: Unfussy Roman cooking a short walk from the museum exit

items.title: Back to the hotel through the heat
items.detail: Late August in Rome peaks around 3pm. Don't fight it.

items.title: Castel Sant'Angelo, then the bridge at sunset
items.detail: Ponte Sant'Angelo with Bernini's angels catching the last light

items.title: Rooftop aperitivo near Campo de' Fiori
OPERA — arias at All Saints' Anglican Church
items.detail: Confirm the Aug 25 programme; Via del Babuino, off Piazza di Spagna

items.title: Late dinner — Pierluigi
items.detail: Seafood on Piazza de' Ricci; a properly Roman hour to eat

days.title: Ancient Rome, end to end
days.note: Last Roman day before the north. The Borghese slot is optional and needs its own timed ticket.

items.title: Colosseum with arena floor, then Forum + Palatine
items.detail: The arena-floor add-on is worth it — you stand where the sand was

items.title: Lunch — Roscioli
items.detail: Carbonara and cacio e pepe, and the deli counter on the way out
items.how: Walk, 5 min via Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Trastevere on foot
items.detail: Cross the Tiber and wander to Piazza Santa Maria in Trastevere

items.title: Optional — Galleria Borghese
items.detail: Timed entry, two-hour slots, books out early. Skip it guilt-free if the day already feels long.

items.title: Dinner — Da Enzo al 29
items.detail: Trastevere, twelve tables, no reservations after 9pm

days.title: North to Florence, by way of Orvieto
days.changeNote: Was Rome → Tuscany. The Orvieto lunch stop survives the swap; it sits on the A1 between Rome and Florence either way.
days.warn: Tight evening. The 8:00pm opera assumes the car reaches Florence by 4pm — hold the driver to a 2:00pm departure from Orvieto. If the drive slips, move the opera to Fri Aug 28 and pull Borgo San Jacopo forward to tonight.

items.title: Check out; collect the car
items.detail: North on the A1

items.title: Orvieto — the Duomo and lunch
items.detail: A hilltop Umbrian town with one of the great striped façades in Italy. Ninety minutes is enough.
items.how: Just off the A1, ~1h15 from Rome

items.title: Back on the road — hold this departure
items.detail: Orvieto → Florence is about two hours

items.title: Check in — Casa G. Firenze
items.detail: Via dei Rondinelli, between the Duomo and Santa Maria Novella

items.title: Unpack and reset
items.detail: You have been in a car since morning

items.title: Aperitivo on the secret patio
items.detail: Casa G.'s courtyard bar

items.title: OPERA — La Traviata at St. Mark's Anglican
items.detail: Via Maggio, across Ponte Santa Trinita — booked for arrival evening, right after the drive from Orvieto.

items.title: Dinner — Trattoria Sostanza
items.detail: Cash only. The butter chicken and the tortino. Alternative: Buca dell'Orafo.

days.title: All of Florence in one day
days.changeNote: Absorbs the Accademia and the Duomo climb from the old arrival day. Three timed entries before lunch — book all three now, in this order.
days.note: Dense by design. Everything before 1pm is ticketed and time-stamped; everything after is yours.

items.title: Accademia — David at first entry
items.detail: Forty-five minutes is genuinely enough. Go straight down the hall.

items.title: Duomo — climb Brunelleschi's dome
items.detail: 463 steps, timed slot, and much better before the day heats up

items.title: Coffee on Piazza della Signoria
items.detail: The Loggia dei Lanzi is an open-air sculpture hall and it is free

items.title: Uffizi, guided
items.detail: Botticelli, Leonardo, the Caravaggio room. Roughly two hours with a guide.

items.title: Lunch in the Oltrarno — Il Santo Bevitore
items.detail: Or Gucci Osteria if you want the splurge. Trattoria Mario is the third option if you'd rather eat near San Lorenzo.

items.title: Pitti Palace and the Boboli Gardens
items.detail: The gardens are the reason to go; climb to the top for the view back over the city

items.title: Oltrarno artisan workshops
items.detail: Via Maggio and Santo Spirito — gilders, leatherworkers, restorers still working street level

items.title: Ponte Vecchio, then up to Piazzale Michelangelo
items.detail: Sunset is around 8:00pm. Taxi up, walk down.

items.title: Dinner — Borgo San Jacopo
items.detail: Michelin-starred, on the river, with a handful of window tables. Ask for one.

days.title: Into the Val d'Elsa, through Certaldo

items.title: Check out; driver southwest
items.detail: Florence → Certaldo is about 45 minutes

items.title: Certaldo Alto, by funicular
items.detail: Boccaccio's birthplace — a walled brick town, the funicular climbs from Piazza Boccaccio in under two minutes

items.title: Casa Boccaccio
items.detail: The Decameron's author was born here; the house is now a small, quiet museum

items.title: Lunch on Via Boccaccio
items.detail: A terrace table in the upper town before the drive on

items.title: On to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes further into the Val d'Elsa

items.title: Check in — Il Castelfalfi
items.detail: A restored 14th-century hamlet on a 2,700-acre estate, its own castle at the centre

items.title: The hamlet on foot
items.detail: The piazza, the castle walls, the little church — all restored, none of it roped off

items.title: Aperitivo at Ecrù
items.detail: The estate's cocktail bar

items.title: Dinner — La Via del Sale
items.detail: The estate's fine-dining room; the vegetables and olive oil are grown on the property

items.title: Driver to San Gimignano
items.detail: About twenty-five minutes

items.title: The towers of San Gimignano
items.detail: Fourteen of the original seventy-two medieval towers still stand — best seen from Piazza della Cisterna

items.title: The Collegiata
items.detail: Ghirlandaio and Gozzoli frescoes wall to wall in a church the size of a chapel

items.title: Gelato at Dondoli
items.detail: A two-time world gelato champion, right on Piazza della Cisterna

items.title: Lunch + a Vernaccia tasting
items.detail: San Gimignano's own DOCG white, crisp and mineral, made for a hot afternoon

items.title: Driver to Volterra
items.detail: About forty-five minutes

items.title: Piazza dei Priori and the Roman theatre
items.detail: Tuscany's most complete medieval civic square, plus a 1st-century BC theatre still being excavated

items.title: Alabaster workshops
items.detail: A carving tradition here since Etruscan times — several studios welcome walk-ins

items.title: Drive back to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About fifty minutes

items.title: Dinner at the resort
items.detail: Or a quieter table down in Montaione village

days.title: Chianti, then the estate
days.note: A slower day by design after two touring days — golf or the spa in the morning, wine after lunch.

items.title: The estate's 27-hole course, or the spa
items.detail: Tuscany's largest golf course, or a morning at the newly renovated spa

items.title: Driver to Montespertoli
items.detail: About forty minutes

items.title: A Chianti Montespertoli estate
items.detail: The smallest Chianti DOCG sub-zone, carved out of the old Colli Fiorentini in 1997 — quieter than Chianti Classico proper

items.title: The village and a second cellar
items.detail: Small enough to see on foot between tastings

items.title: Back to Castelfalfi
items.detail: About forty minutes

items.title: The pool or the spa terrace at sunset
Dinner — Giglio Blu or La Via del Sale
items.detail: Something casual, or a second night at the estate's fine-dining room

days.title: The long haul south
days.warn: The longest drive of the trip — about 4.5 hours of highway before you've even reached Pompeii. Swap drivers if you can, fill the tank before you leave Castelfalfi, and expect Naples-area traffic to eat into the buffer.

items.title: Check out; on the road early
items.detail: South on the A1 — Florence's ring road, then the long autostrada stretch past Rome and Caserta

items.title: Fuel and coffee stop
items.detail: An Autogrill service area north of Rome — top up the tank, swap drivers

items.title: Toward Naples and Pompeii
items.detail: The A1 becomes the A2 past Rome; exit for Pompei Scavi

items.title: Pompeii, guided
items.detail: Two hours is the right length in September heat. Ask for the Villa of the Mysteries. Parking is at the Pompei Scavi lot by the entrance.

items.title: Snack, then onto the corniche
items.detail: The coast road starts properly after Vietri — narrow, slow, spectacular. Take it easy.

items.title: Check in — Anantara Convento di Amalfi
items.detail: A 13th-century monastery on the cliff edge, with the original cloister still standing

items.title: Dinner — Dei Cappuccini
items.detail: The hotel's Michelin room, or La Locanda for pizza if the day has beaten you

days.title: Capri, by private boat
days.note: Weather-dependent. The Blue Grotto only opens in a flat sea — treat it as a bonus, not a plan.

items.title: Private boat from the hotel jetty
items.detail: Lucibello, roughly seven hours with skipper

items.title: The Faraglioni, the grottoes, the swim coves
items.detail: Blue Grotto if the sea is calm enough to enter

items.title: Lunch — Da Paolino
items.detail: Under the lemon trees. Il Riccio is the Michelin alternative, on the cliff by the grotto.

items.title: The Piazzetta and the Gardens of Augustus
items.detail: Gelato on the terrace above Via Krupp

items.title: Cruise home, prosecco at sunset
items.detail: About forty minutes back along the coast

items.title: Dinner — La Conca del Sogno
items.detail: Reachable by boat, in a cove near Nerano. Or stay in on the cloister terrace.

days.title: Ravello, above everything
days.note: The Ravello Festival runs to Sep 5. Check tonight's programme — the stage is built out over the cliff at Villa Rufolo. The switchbacks up from the coast are tight and slow to self-drive; if you'd rather not, the hotel can call a local driver for this one leg.

items.title: The beach club, by cliff lift
items.detail: A slow morning at sea level before the day starts properly

items.title: Lunch — Lo Scoglio
items.detail: Nerano. The original spaghetti alla Nerano, and worth the boat ride on its own.

items.title: Up to Ravello
items.detail: Forty-five minutes of switchbacks above the coast

items.title: Villa Cimbrone
items.detail: The Terrace of Infinity — a marble balustrade lined with busts, and a thousand-foot drop to the sea

items.title: RAVELLO FESTIVAL — check the Sep 3 programme
items.detail: Confirmed concerts run to Sep 5. The Aug 29 Mahler Youth Orchestra date falls on your Florence → Siena transfer, so it is out either way.

items.title: Late dinner — Il Flauto di Pan
items.detail: In the Villa Cimbrone gardens. Rossellinis is the other option.

items.title: Check out; last look at the coast
Drive to Naples
items.detail: Coast road, then the A3, ~1.5 hrs

items.title: Check in — De Bonart, Curio Collection
items.detail: An art palazzo on Via Partenope in Chiaia, facing the bay. Use the hotel's valet — Naples is not a city for a rental car to sit unattended.

items.title: Naples Archaeological Museum
items.detail: Where everything good from Pompeii actually ended up. Go after seeing the site, not before.

items.title: Spaccanapoli
items.detail: The dead-straight Greek road that still splits the old city in half

items.title: Street food, standing up
items.detail: Pizza fritta, zeppoline, a sfogliatella riccia straight from the oven

items.title: Rooftop aperitivo
items.detail: Vesuvius on one side, the bay on the other

items.title: Dinner — Palazzo Petrucci
items.detail: Michelin-starred Neapolitan tasting menu

items.title: Pizza for breakfast
items.detail: Sorbillo or Di Matteo on Via dei Tribunali. Yes, at 9am. It's Naples.

items.title: Collect the car; on the road
items.detail: Naples → Rome is about two and a half hours on the A1

items.title: Check in — The St. Regis Rome
items.detail: The hotel is inside Rome's ZTL — use valet or a garage nearby; don't try to park at the curb.

items.title: Last Roman afternoon
items.detail: Piazza di Spagna and the windows along Via Condotti

items.title: Aperitivo at Lumen
items.detail: The St. Regis bar — the grand-hotel version of a last night

items.title: Farewell dinner — Aroma
items.detail: A rooftop table level with the top tier of the Colosseum. Imago is the alternative, over the Spanish Steps.

days.title: Arrivederci
days.warn: The rental is booked for a 12:00pm drop-off, but the flight leaves at 10:20am — the car would still be at FCO after you've taken off. Call the rental company and move the drop-off to around 6:00am.

items.title: Drive to FCO; drop off the car
items.detail: About forty minutes on an empty Sunday road — reservation #21586310US4

items.title: Check in and bag drop
items.detail: Three hours ahead for an intercontinental departure

items.title: FCO → IAH
items.detail: Arrivederci, Italia.

hotels.name: Hotel Trame
hotels.blurb: A former Franciscan monastery two streets from Campo de' Fiori.

hotels.name: Casa G. Firenze
hotels.blurb: Via dei Rondinelli, midway between the Duomo and Santa Maria Novella.

hotels.name: Il Castelfalfi
hotels.blurb: A restored 14th-century hamlet on a 2,700-acre estate, with Tuscany's largest golf course and its own vineyards.

hotels.name: Anantara Convento di Amalfi
hotels.blurb: A 13th-century monastery on the cliff, cloister intact.

hotels.name: De Bonart Naples
hotels.blurb: An art palazzo on Via Partenope, facing the bay.

hotels.name: The St. Regis Rome
hotels.blurb: Five minutes from Termini, for one grand last night.

drivers.route: FCO → garage near Hotel Trame, Rome
Rome → Orvieto (lunch stop) → Casa G. Firenze, Florence
drivers.note: Florence ZTL ~€200 if you drive into the centro storico
The longest drive of the trip — start early and swap drivers
Tight switchbacks — a local driver is a fine substitute for this one leg
Use the hotel valet in Naples

drivers.route: De Bonart Naples → The St. Regis Rome

drivers.note: Drop-off is booked for noon — move it earlier so it isn't after the flight

driversNote: The IDP ships by Aug 3 — pack it with the physical licence, not just a photo of it. Rome and Florence's historic centres are ZTL zones: enter only to check in/out, then park in a garage just outside (Rome ~€35–45/night, Florence ~€30–35/night) and walk. Castelfalfi and the Amalfi hotel have their own parking. Budget roughly €80 in tolls for the full route and a full tank about every 2–3 driving days.

bookings.item: Book Casa G. Firenze for Aug 27–29
bookings.detail: Two nights in Florence, wedged between Rome and Tuscany — the tightest hotel window on the trip.

bookings.item: Reserve dinners at Il Castelfalfi — La Via del Sale, Aug 29 & 31
bookings.detail: The estate's fine-dining room. Worth booking ahead even though the room itself is already confirmed.

bookings.item: Fix the rental car's drop-off time
bookings.detail: Reservation #21586310US4 has drop-off at noon on Sep 6, but the flight leaves at 10:20am. Call and move it to around 6:00am.

bookings.item: Plan Rome and Florence parking before you land
bookings.detail: Both hotels sit inside a ZTL — pick a garage just outside each one now, rather than improvising on arrival with a rental car and jet lag.

bookings.item: Florence opera — La Traviata at St. Mark's, Aug 27
bookings.detail: Lands the same evening as the Orvieto drive north — the fallback is Aug 28 if the drive runs late.

bookings.item: Rome opera — All Saints' Anglican, Aug 25
bookings.detail: Confirm the programme is posted before booking.

bookings.item: Montespertoli estate visit for Mon Aug 31
bookings.detail: A Chianti Montespertoli producer, plus lunch — most require an appointment rather than taking walk-ins.

bookings.item: Timed entries — Accademia, Duomo dome, Uffizi, all on Aug 28
bookings.detail: Three in one morning, in that order. Book the dome climb first; it has the fewest slots.

bookings.item: Vatican early entry (Aug 25), Colosseum arena floor (Aug 26), Pompeii guide (Sep 1)
bookings.detail: All three need booking — the Vatican and Colosseum slots go first.
Roughly seven hours with a skipper from the hotel jetty — book a few weeks out in peak season.

bookings.item: Ravello Festival — check the Sep 3 programme
bookings.detail: Festival runs to Sep 5. The confirmed Aug 29 Mahler date falls on your Florence→Castelfalfi transfer, so it was never reachable.
Sostanza Aug 27 · Borgo San Jacopo Aug 28 · La Via del Sale Aug 29 & 31 · San Gimignano lunch Aug 30. Plus Armando, Roscioli, Lo Scoglio — reserve ahead where they take bookings.

bookingsRuledOut.reason: Needs a Verona overnight; Sep 4 is the Amalfi → Naples transfer.

budget.note: 6 hotels, 13 nights. Trame, Castelfalfi and Convento are actual quotes.
Rental car $1,175 (€1,087.81, actual), plus fuel, tolls, ZTL/garage parking.
Vatican, Colosseum, Pompeii, Capri boat, wineries, Florence galleries, operas.
Taxis, tips, Naples street food, incidentals.

photographers.spots: Pincio terrace and Villa Borghese at sunset; the Colosseum and Trevi at dawn, empty; the Spanish Steps
Piazzale Michelangelo at sunset; Ponte Vecchio at dawn; the Uffizi loggia
San Gimignano's towers at golden hour; the Castelfalfi vineyards and golf course; Volterra's alabaster studios
Positano's pastel stairs and Spiaggia Grande; Amalfi Drive viewpoints; the Ravello gardens
Gardens of Augustus over the Faraglioni; Via Krupp; Marina Grande

photographersNote: Trip.com has no reliable Italy 旅拍 listings. Book through Flytographer or Localgrapher and request a Mandarin-speaking photographer in the notes, or find 旅拍 photographers directly on 小红书 using the searches above. Shoot dawn for empty landmarks, golden hour for the coast and the Tuscan hills.
